game_info.title: Lord of the Rings Galaxy — Rules & Lore Database
game_info.description: Rules and lore for a Lord of the Rings themed space-faring galaxy, reimagining Middle-earth as a star-spanning galaxy with constellations as star systems, the Valar as planets, and the Rings of Power as galactic artifacts.
source_materials: The Lord of the Rings by J.R.R. Tolkien (1954-1955)

ground_combat.source: Adapted from Star Wars: Legion and similar miniatures wargames
ground_combat.description: Miniatures-based ground combat with alternating activations and command cards, adapted for the armies of the Arda galaxy.

command_phase.description: Both players secretly select a command card, then reveal and resolve effects. Priority is determined by comparing pip values.
steps: Each player selects a command card from their hand and places it face-down
Both players reveal command cards simultaneously
Resolve command card effects
Compare pip values to determine priority
The priority player issues orders first

activation_phase.description: Players alternate activating units. Each unit can move, shoot, and/or charge.
steps: Active player selects a unit with an order token
Unit may move up to its speed value
Unit may shoot at enemies in range (roll attack dice)
Unit may charge into melee if within charge range
Resolve melee combat (both units roll attack dice)
Remove order token; unit is exhausted until next round

melee_phase.description: Units in melee engagement resolve combat.
steps: All units in melee roll attack dice simultaneously
Resolve hits and damage
Push back effects are resolved
Eliminated units are removed

order_types.advance: Unit moves toward the enemy; gains +1 attack dice in melee
order_types.hold: Unit does not move; gains +1 defense dice
order_types.flank: Unit moves to the side; can outflank enemy positions
order_types.ambush: Unit hides and strikes from cover; first strike advantage

space_combat.description: Space combat uses secret maneuver planning with dials, firing arcs, and dice-based attacks, adapted for the starships of the Arda galaxy.

movement_phase.description: Players secretly select maneuvers, then reveal and execute them simultaneously.
steps: Each player secretly selects a maneuver from their maneuver dial
Both players reveal maneuvers simultaneously
Execute maneuvers: move ships according to dial selection
Resolve collisions and overlap (push back later-moving ship)

action_phase.description: Players alternate performing actions with their ships.
actions: Focus (gain focus token; converts to hit or adds defense dice)
Evade (gain evade token; adds defense dice when targeted)
Lock (target an enemy for special weapons)

attack_phase.description: Ships in firing arc resolve attacks.
steps: Attacker declares target in firing arc
Roll attack dice (modified by range, abilities, and focus)
Defender rolls defense dice (modified by evade and abilities)
Resolve hits: assign damage cards face-down
Resolve critical hits: reveal damage cards face-up

firing_arcs.front_arc: Most ships can only attack in their front 120-degree arc
firing_arcs.full_arc: Some ships (e.g., Elven Ships, Barad-dûr) can attack in any direction
firing_arcs.rear_arc: Some specialized weapons can fire backward

galaxy_control.description: Galaxy-scale control game. The Free Peoples and Forces of Darkness compete for control of star systems across the Arda galaxy.

structure: Strategic Movement Phase — move fleets between systems
Action Selection Phase — secretly select action cards
Action Resolution Phase — resolve actions in order
Regroup Phase — draw cards, place resources, ready units

actions.space_combat: Engage in space combat in a star system
actions.ground_combat: Deploy ground forces to determine system loyalty
actions.espionage: Sabotage enemy systems or steal resources
actions.pass: Skip your turn; gain a resource

victory_conditions.free_peoples: Destroy the One Ring in Mount Doom OR control 6 systems with 3+ influence
victory_conditions.forces_of_darkness: Find and capture the Ring-bearer OR control 8 systems with 3+ influence

system_types.special: Unique effects (e.g., Mount Doom, Valinor, the Shire)

ring_mechanics.description: The One Ring is a central game mechanic. Its location and bearer affect the entire game.

ring_bearer.description: The Ring-bearer is a hidden unit that must reach Mount Doom. The Forces of Darkness seek to find and capture the Ring-bearer.
mechanics: The Ring-bearer is hidden from the Forces of Darkness
The Forces of Darkness can use the Palantíri and the Eye to search for the Ring-bearer
If the Ring-bearer is captured, the Forces of Darkness win
If the Ring-bearer reaches Mount Doom, the Free Peoples win
The Ring corrupts the bearer over time — a corruption track must be managed

corruption_track.description: The Ring-bearer has a corruption track. If it fills, the Ring-bearer claims the Ring and the Forces of Darkness win.
stages: Tempted — minor penalties; the Ring grows heavier
Burdened — significant penalties; the Ring is very heavy
Weakened — severe penalties; the Ring-bearer may need assistance
Claimed — the Ring-bearer claims the Ring; Forces of Darkness win

palantir_mechanics.description: The Palantíri are seeing-stones that allow communication and surveillance across the galaxy.
mechanics: Players with Palantíri can communicate across any distance
Sauron's Palantíri can be used to search for the Ring-bearer
Using a Palantír risks being dominated by Sauron
Aragorn's Palantír can be used to deceive Sauron

narrative_elements.description: The game includes narrative elements reflecting Tolkien's themes of hope, destiny, and the power of small acts of courage.

fate_cards.description: Fate cards represent the hand of destiny in the game. They can be drawn at critical moments.
examples: The Riders Arrive — Rohan reinforcements appear at a critical moment
The Entmoot — the Ents decide to march on Isengard
The Council of Elrond — the Fellowship is formed
The Breaking of the Fellowship — the Fellowship is scattered
The Last Ark — the final stand at the Black Gates
The Grey Havens — the Ring-bearers depart for Valinor

hope_mechanic.description: Hope is a resource that the Free Peoples can build and spend. It represents the power of small acts of courage.
mechanics: Hope is generated by successful actions and heroic deeds
Hope can be spent to reroll dice, gain extra actions, or activate Fate cards
Hope is lost when units are eliminated or systems fall
If hope reaches zero, the Free Peoples suffer severe penalties
